subject: Next week classwork
text: Hello everyone, I am writing about next week's reading assignment and the short reflection due Friday. The deadline feels tight because several of us are still working through last week's discussion notes, and the library copy is overdue. I suggest we split the source material into three equal parts instead of asking each person to summarize the whole chapter. If that works, one person can handle pages one through twelve, I can take pages thirteen through twenty-four, and a third can finish pages twenty-five through thirty-six. Please bring your pages to the Wednesday meeting rather than trying to finish everything at home. We will need a shared folder, but I can create it tonight if someone confirms they can upload scans or photos by tomorrow lunch. If anyone has the digital handout, send it now so we stop duplicating effort. My main concern is that we do not submit three unrelated mini-reports that miss the question in the prompt. Let us spend the first fifteen minutes comparing notes, then outline the main argument together. Reply by tonight. If someone cannot attend Wednesday, send two sentences before nine a.m. so I can include them in the shared outline. We should decide whether to cite the documentary or focus on articles. I lean toward the articles because the instructions mention primary documents, but I am open to a short film reference if we can tie it back. Please do not wait until Thursday night; that means rushed paragraphs and missing page numbers.
